To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incorporation of tritium-labeled thymidine into DNA results in neoplastic transformation of Syrian hamster embryo cells.

(methyl-/sub 3/H) thymidine incorporation into DNA of Syrian hamster embryo cells causes morphological transformation and that this transformation is accompanied by increased expression of neoplastic phenotypic markers, including tumorigenicity, enhanced fibrinolysis, and anchorage-independent growth.
(methyl-/ sup 3/H)TdR incorporation into DNA of normal cells induces neoplastic transformation, and that this transformation is associated with specific DNA/nuclear alterations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system for the study and analysis of neoplastic cell transformation.
the study of neoplasm induction and its relation to DNA damage and somatic mutation.
the study of the mechanism by which the incorporation of (/sup 14/C or (/sup 3/)H)thymidine into DNA induces neoplastic transformation of normal cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tritiated thimidine incorporation into the DNA of a normal cell can induce neoplastic transformation in that cell.
the incorporation of (/sup 2/H)thymdine into DNA of normal hamster embryo cells leads to the development of transformed cells which exhibit a variety of neoplastic properties.
the present study demonstrates that incorporation of (/sup 2/H)thymine results in a specific and dose-dependent neoplastic transformation of normal diploid hamster embryo cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the incorporation of (/sup 14/C)thymidine into the DNA of normal diploid hamster embryo fiboblasts results in the induction of specific neoplasms, which display a number of characteristic phenotypic changes.
the incorporation of (/sup 2/H)thymine into DNA of normal cells can lead to the development of transformed cells.
the incorporation of (5-/super 3/H) thymidine results in DNA damage, which is manifested by the induction of specific neoplasia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA damage induced by (methyl-/ sup 3/H)Tdr is sufficient to induce neoplastic transformation of hamster embryo fibrobasts (HEFs).
tritium incorporation can cause mutations in the DNA of cells, and that these mutations can be passed on to daughter cells.
tritium is a potent mutagen and carcinogen, and that the effects can occur at levels of tritium that are not detectable by standard methods.
